paragraphs: Friend, I know a list of names looks like the part of the Bible where you check your phone. But look at what David is doing here. He is setting up order for the house of the LORD, and the priests get twenty-four families and twenty-four turns. Nobody got to shove to the front, because the order was settled by lot.

Now watch how the turns get handed out. They cast lots in the presence of the king, and Eleazar's bigger side and Ithamar's smaller side go into the same drawing. The reason is that there were "officers of the sanctuary and officers of God among both" (1 Chronicles 24:5). Then the other Levite families cast lots too, and the family heads and their "younger brothers alike" (1 Chronicles 24:31) all take part, so bigger side or smaller side, oldest or youngest, nobody gets waved off.

Here's what that means for you, baker. Serving God is not a spot reserved for the biggest names. Each of the twenty-four priestly families got a turn, and the scribe wrote their names down in front of the king (1 Chronicles 24:6). Also, this order followed what "the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded" Aaron (1 Chronicles 24:19), so it was never just David's bright idea. Your turn to serve is real and it counts, and I'm saying that as a stamper who once sat in a drawer thinking nobody would ever call his number.
